newsitem.title: USA: Bankers Trust uses new financing structure.
newsitem.headline: Bankers Trust uses new financing structure.

text.p: Federal National Mortgage Association (Fannie Mae) said on Wednesday Bankers Trust New York Corp sold a $224 million portfolio of affordable multifamily loans by Fannie Mae's new financing structure.

The new Wisconsin Avenue Securities Real Estate Mortgage Investment Conduit (REMIC) structure provides faster and easier execution, at lower costs, than Fannie Mae's previous REMIC structure, the company said.
Bankers Trust swapped the portfolio of loans, which included 117 properties in 27 states, for a Fannie Mae REMIC, Fannie Mae said.
A REMIC is a multiple-class mortgage cash flow security backed by mortgage loans that restructures interest and principal payments into separately traded securities, Fannie Mae said.
Under the new structure, Fannie Mae creates a single REMIC consisting of senior bonds that are guaranteed by Fannie Mae and subordinate bonds that are unguaranteed, Fannie Mae said.
